## `OauthGrantType`

The method by which the access token will be obtained. The Everpure REST API supports the OAuth 2.0 "token exchange" grant type, which indicates that a token exchange is being performed. Set `grant_type` to `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`.

Type: string

## `OauthSubjectToken`

An encoded security ID Token representing the identity of the party on behalf of whom the request is being made. The token must be issued by a trusted identity provider which must be either a registered application in Pure1 or an enabled API client on the array. The token must be a JSON Web Token and must contain the following claims: > \| JWT claim \| Location \| API Client Field \| Description…

Type: string

## `OauthSubjectTokenType`

An identifier that indicates the type of security token specifed in the `subject_token` parameter. The Everpure REST API supports the JSON Web Token (JWT) as the means for requesting the access token. Set `subject_token_type` to `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt`.

Type: string

## `ResourceAccess`

A resource access captures configuration of sharing a resource to a scope. For example, resource access can specify that an array host is accessible from a realm.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (read-only) | ID of a resource access object. |
| `resource` | `_referenceWithType` | Resource to which the scope has access. |
| `scope` | `_referenceWithType` | Scope which has access to the resource. |

## `ResourceAccessStatus`

A resource access status realizes the configuration of resource accesses. For instance, if there is a resource access for a host group to a realm, resource access status would include the explicit host group resource access as well as an implicit resource access for each host in that host group.

|---|---|---|
| `created_by` | array of `ResourceAccessStatusCreatedBy` (read-only) | Reference the IDs of resource accesses that created this status. |
| `resource` | `_referenceWithType` | Resource to which the scope has access. |
| `scope` | `_referenceWithType` | Scope which has access to the resource. |

## `_presetWorkloadBase`

Workload presets are reusable templates that provision workloads.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bucket_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadBucketConfiguration` | The object store buckets that will be provisioned by the preset. |
| `description` | string | A brief description of the workload the preset will configure. Supports up to 1KB of unicode characters. |
| `directory_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadDirectoryConfiguration` | The file systems and managed directories that will be provisioned by the preset. |
| `export_configurations` | `_presetWorkloadExportConfigurations` | The NFS, SMB, and SMB share policy configuration specified in file system and directory exports. |

| `placement_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadPlacementConfiguration` | The placement configurations that can be applied to storage resources (such as volumes) within the preset. All storage resources associated with the same placement will be colocated on the same array. |
| `platform_features` | array of `_presetWorkloadPlatformFeatures` |  |
| `qos_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadQosConfiguration` | The QoS configurations that can be applied to storage resources (such as volumes) within the preset. |

| `revision` | integer (int64) (read-only) | A counter that is automatically incremented by the server when the preset is updated. |
| `snapshot_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadSnapshotConfiguration` | The snapshot configurations that can be applied to storage resources (such as volumes) within the preset. |
| `volume_configurations` | array of `_presetWorkloadVolumeConfiguration` | The volumes that will be provisioned by the preset. |
| `workload_tags` | array of `_presetWorkloadWorkloadTag` | The tags that will be associated with workloads provisioned by the preset. |

|---|---|---|
| `all_for_sec` | integer (int32) | The length of time to keep the specified snapshots. Measured in seconds. Prior to 6.8.2 the range of 60 to 34560000 is accepted. In 6.8.2 and onwards the range of 60 to 2147483647 is accepted. |
| `days` | integer (int32) | The number of days to keep the snapshots after the `all_for_sec` period has passed. Prior to 6.6.4 the range of 0 to 4000 is accepted. In 6.6.4 and onwards the range of 0 to 2147483647 is accepted. In 6.10.0 and… |
| `per_day` | integer (int32) | Deprecated. per_day is deprecated in favor of per_period and period_length_ms. The number of snapshots to keep per day after the `all_for_sec` period has passed. Prior to 6.8.2 the range of 0 to 1440 is accepted. In… |
| `per_period` | integer (int32) | The number of snapshots to keep per period_length_ms after the `all_for_sec` period has passed. The range of 0 to 2147483647 is accepted. |
| `period_length_ms` | integer (int64) | The length of time per_period should cover. Measured in milliseconds. Must be a multiple of 86400000 to represent a whole number of days. A minimum of 86400000, 1 day, is accepted. |

## `_workloadConfigurationReferencePatch`

The instruction for removing the resource from the workload. Setting the `id` or `name` of the workload to an empty string (`""`) removes the resource.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified. |
| `name` | string | The resource name, such as volume name, pod name, snapshot name, and so on. |

## `_workloadConfigurationReferencePost`

The workload to which the resource is added. Set one of `id` or `name`, and `configuration` to add the resource to the workload and configure it based on the `configuration` from the preset revision the workload was originally provisioned from.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified. |
| `name` | string | The resource name, such as volume name, pod name, snapshot name, and so on. |
| `resource_type` | string (read-only) | Type of the object (full name of the endpoint). Valid values are `hosts`, `host-groups`, `network-interfaces`, `pods`, `ports`, `pod-replica-links`, `realms`, `subnets`, `volumes`, `volume-snapshots`, `volume-groups`,… |
| `configuration` | string | The name of the preset configuration object. |

The name and value of a single parameter.

## `_workloadParameterValue`

The value of the parameter.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `boolean` | boolean | The value for a boolean parameter. |
| `integer` | integer (int64) | The value for an integer parameter. |
| `resource_reference` | `_workloadParameterValueResourceReference` | The value for a resource reference parameter. |
| `string` | string | The value for a string parameter. |

## `_workloadParameterValueResourceReference`

The value for a resource reference parameter.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The id of the resource to reference. One of `id` or `name` must be set, but they cannot be set together. |
| `name` | string | The name of the resource to reference. One of `id` or `name` must be set, but they cannot be set together. |
| `resource_type` | string | The type of the resource to reference. Resource type is optional, and will be automatically determined by the server if not set. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationAdditionalConstraints`

The list of targets considered for workload placement must satisfy the requirements imposed by the `preset`. Users can also specify additional `constraints` to further restrict the list of targets for consideration.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `required_resource_references` | array of `_workloadPlacementRecommendationResourceReference` | The property that defines a group of resources. At least one resource from each item must be present on the `target` for it to be considered an acceptable candidate for workload placement. |
| `targets` | array of `_referenceWithType` | The list of `targets` to consider when computing placement recommendations. If not specified, the entire fleet is used to compute the recommendation. Specify `targets` as individual arrays or as topology groups by… |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationGenericTarget`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `end` | number (float) | The projection for the end of the projection period. Length of the projection period is defined by 'projection_months'. The percentage is displayed as a decimal value, starting at 0.00 and ending at 1.00. |
| `start` | number (float) | The projection for the start of the projection period (i.e., immediately after the creation of the workload on this target). The percentage is displayed as a decimal value, starting at 0.00 and ending at 1.00. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationResourceReference`

Defines a group of resources. At least one of them should be present on this target to use it for computation of a recommendation. Currently only hosts or host groups could be used.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allowed_values` | array of `_referenceWithType` | A list of allowed values for the resource reference. For hosts and host groups, each item does not define a specific object on some target, but defines a pattern which should be matched by the target. For example, {… |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationResult`

Single workload placement recommendation result.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `parameters` | array of `_workloadParameter` | The parameter values passed to the preset when creating a workload based on the recommendation result. |
| `placements` | array of `_workloadPlacementRecommendationPlacement` (read-only) | The placements of the preset. (Deprecated) Use 'targets' instead. |
| `score` | string (read-only) | The score of the recommendation from Pure1. Possible values include `optimal`, `optimal-with-warnings`, and `acceptable`. |
| `targets` | array of `_workloadPlacementRecommendationGenericTarget` (read-only) | The list of recommended arrays. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationTarget`

Data for a target in a workload placement recommendation. Target is a FlashArray, which may be used for workload placement.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified. |
| `name` | string | The resource name, such as volume name, pod name, snapshot name, and so on. |
| `resource_type` | string | Type of the object (full name of the endpoint). Valid values are `hosts`, `host-groups`, `network-interfaces`, `pods`, `ports`, `pod-replica-links`, `subnets`, `volumes`, `volume-snapshots`, `volume-groups`,… |
| `capacity` | integer (int64) | The usable capacity of the target, measured in bytes. |
| `capacity_used_projections` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationTargetCapacityUsedProjections` | Projections for the capacity consumed by customer data. |
| `load_projections` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationTargetLoadProjections` | Load depicts the storage system utilization as a percentage from 0, when the system is completely idle, to 100, when the system is completely saturated. |
| `model` | string | The model of the target. For example, `FA-X20R2`. |
| `warnings` | array of `_workloadPlacementRecommendationWarning` | The warnings for the target. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationTargetCapacityUsedProjections`

Projections for the capacity consumed by customer data.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `days_until_full` | integer (int32) | The number of days until the target is at full capacity. |
| `projection` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection` | The projection of the used capacity, assuming the workload is provisioned on this target. |
| `projection_baseline` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection` | The projection of the baseline used capacity, without the workload on this target. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationTargetLoadProjections`

Load depicts the storage system utilization as a percentage from 0, when the system is completely idle, to 100, when the system is completely saturated.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `projection_avg` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection` | The projected average load on the target. |
| `projection_baseline` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection` | The projected baseline load on the target, without the workload on this target. |
| `projection_blended_max` | `_workloadPlacementRecommendationProjection` | The projected blended maximum load on the target. |

## `_workloadPlacementRecommendationWarning`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | The warning code. Possible values include `limit_volumes_count`, `limit_pods_count`, etc. |
| `message` | string | The warning message. Possible values include `Adding the workload on the array would exceed the limit on volumes`, `Adding the workload on the array would exceed the limit on pods`, etc. |

## `_workloadPreset`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (read-only) | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified. |
| `name` | string (read-only) | The resource name, such as volume name, file system name, snapshot name, and so on. |
| `resource_type` | string (read-only) | Type of the object (full name of the endpoint). Valid values are the unique part of the resource's REST endpoint. For example, a reference to a file system would have a `resource_type` of `file-systems`. |
| `revision` | integer (int64) (read-only) | The revision of the preset from which the workload was deployed. |
